name: Question 2
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2{e}^{2t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x={e}^{2}$ and velocity $v={e}^{2}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2{e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & ={e}^{2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & ={e}^{2(1)}+C \\ {e}^{2} & ={e}^{2}+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)={e}^{2t}.$ 

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{2t}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(1)={e}^{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2(1)}+K \\ {e}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+K \\ K & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}.
$$

Question 2
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=2e2t, where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=e2 and velocity v=e2 when t=1, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=2e2t+te2+12e2
b
x(t)=2e2t+e2
c
x(t)=e2t+te2
d
x(t)=12e2t+12e2
e
x(t)=12e2t+te2+e2
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity v(t):

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫2e2tdt=e2t+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=e2. Substituting this into the above gives

e2=e2(1)+Ce2=e2+CC=0.

So the velocity is given by v(t)=e2t.

Now, we integrate the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫e2tdt=12e2t+K

To determine K, we use the fact that x(1)=e2. Substituting this into the above gives

e2=12e2(1)+Ke2=12e2+KK=12e2.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=12e2t+12e2.
